root.claim: Two $n$-bit integers can be multiplied exactly by a deterministic multitape machine in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: reduce multiplication through a chain of convolution problems down to polynomial-ring convolution, evaluated with the fast tape procedures

motivation.text: The standard transform-based approach costs n log n at best; the chain of reductions puts the problem in a form where transforms are made only of address moves, shifts and butterflies, which the two fast procedures speed up by a power of log n.

adds.name: saving exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed constant giving the power saving $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$ over $n\lg n$.

children.method: construct each procedure from a linear network and extract a power saving

children.claim: Address interchange of two $u$-bit fields of an array of stored bit volume $V$ costs $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$, using XOR combinations of data.
children.method: build a fixed linear network with frames, restore auxiliaries, and recurse on a strict call-count inequality

motivation.text: A direct scan costs a full pass per level; a network whose edges are smaller calls of the same procedure lets a strict inequality on call counts compound into a power saving.

children.salient: The exponent tau is strictly below 1 although the final effect is an exact permutation built only of XOR combinations.
